name: Kryt'-Navalivat' (Крыть-наваливать)
description: Kryt'-Navalivat' (Russian for 'Covering and Piling Up') is a traditional Russian card game for two players, although it can accommodate more. It is a descendant of the 'Durak' (Fool) family, specifically influenced by 'Duraki s nakladkoy'. The game focuses on the tactical choice between beating a card (Covering) and forcing more cards onto the opponent (Piling Up). The objective is to empty your hand; the last player left with cards is the 'Fool'.

content.text: Kryt'-Navalivat' (Russian for 'Covering and Piling Up') is a traditional Russian card game for two players, although it can accommodate more. It is a descendant of the 'Durak' (Fool) family, specifically influenced by 'Duraki s nakladkoy'. The game focuses on the tactical choice between beating a card (Covering) and forcing more cards onto the opponent (Piling Up). The objective is to empty your hand; the last player left with cards is the 'Fool'.
Originates in 18th-century Russia, predating the modern standardized 'Podkidnoy Durak'. It belongs to the 'Nakladka' branch of games which emphasizes the volume of cards in the play pile.
2 players is the standard competitive format.

items.text: Duraki s nakladkoy: The direct parent game with more complex piling rules.
Vsyak svoi kozyri: A variant where each player chooses their own trump suit.
Podkidnoy Durak: The modern international standard.
